learn.title: Moving shapes
learn.body: A transformation moves a figure. Three kinds keep the size and shape exactly the same: a translation slides it, a reflection flips it over a line, and a rotation turns it around a point. The new figure is congruent to the old one.

learn.title: Rules on the coordinate plane
learn.body: Translation by $(a,b)$: $(x,y)\to(x+a,y+b)$. Reflection over the $x$-axis: $(x,y)\to(x,-y)$. Reflection over the $y$-axis: $(x,y)\to(-x,y)$. Reflection over the line $y=x$: $(x,y)\to(y,x)$.

learn.title: Rotations about the origin
learn.body: Counterclockwise $90^\circ$: $(x,y)\to(-y,x)$. Clockwise $90^\circ$: $(x,y)\to(y,-x)$. Half turn $180^\circ$: $(x,y)\to(-x,-y)$. A rotation keeps every point the same distance from the centre.
All three keep distances and angles unchanged, so the image is congruent to the original.

questions.prompt: Translate $(1,1)$ by $(2,3)$. What is the new $x$-coordinate?
Rotate $(3,2)$ by $90^\circ$ counterclockwise about the origin.

questions.explanation: A half turn changes both signs.
